overview: The Small Business Administration (SBA) has an Office of Veterans Business Development that supports businesses owned by veterans. A 1999 law, the Veterans Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development Act, includes reporting requirements related to veteran-owned small businesses. As the bill's title notes, the Government Accountability Office (GAO), Congress's nonpartisan auditing agency, has made recommendations to the SBA in this area. This short bill would require the head of the SBA's veterans business office to put in place policies and procedures within 60 days to make sure the agency meets those existing reporting requirements. As of October 9, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar for a vote.
for: Supporters say the SBA should follow reporting rules already in law, and that reliable reports help Congress understand how well veteran-owned businesses are being served.
against: Critics say the bill only tells an agency to obey an existing law and adds no new tools or resources, so it may do little to change results for veteran business owners.
